question.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
question.text: This Holy Roman Emperor, third of the Salian dynasty, was involved in the Investiture Controversy with the Papacy and stood in the snow for three days begging for forgiveness.
question.clue: His first wife was spurned in favor of his mistress Gabrielle d'Estrees, who bore this victim of Francois Ravaillac four children.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Luebeck ended the Danish involvement in this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict that began with the Bohemian Revolt and the Defenestration of Prague and primarily pitted the Hapsburgs and their allies against the Bourbons and their allies.
swap.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

question.text: The Utraquists' insistence on serving both the bread and the wine during the Eucharist contributed to a series of conflicts named for this Bohemian religious leader, who was executed at the Council of Constance.
question.clue: This author of De Ecclesia allegedly told his executors that a swan would avenge him in one hundred years even though he was presently a "roasted goose," a play on his name.

swap.text: After the Council of Constance, these wars were fought against Bohemians who followed the teachings of a namesake Czech reformer. Until his death, Jan Zizka led the radical Taborite faction to victories in these wars.
swap.clue: Raids called "beautiful rides" were conducted by Prokop the Great in this conflict, which ended at the Battle of Lipany where the Utraquists defeated the Taborites.

question.leadin: This emperor convened the Diet of Roncaglia after crushing Milan.
question.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor, who drowned in the Saleph River. He is nicknamed for his red beard.
question.answerHtml: Frederick Barbarossa [accept Frederick I; prompt on Frederick or Barbarossa alone]
question.clue: This man's body was preserved in a barrel of vinegar after this man had drowned in the Saleph River whilst leading his armies to the Third Crusade.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Thirty Years' War.
swap.text: The Bohemian period of the Thirty Years' War was ended by this 1620 battle near Prague, in which the Count of Tilly defeated Protestant forces lead by Christian of Anhalt.
swap.clue: As a result of this engagement, the nephew of James I of England and ruler of the Palatinate earned the epithet "Winter King," as it ended the rule of Frederick V after less than one year.

question.leadin: 27 leaders of one revolt named for this historic region were executed in the Old Town Square of its capital.
question.text: Name this historic region in which Protestants revolted against Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II in 1618. That revolt began after two of the emperor's representatives were defenestrated in this historic region's capital.
question.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

swap.text: The first king of newly independent Greece was a Bavarian prince of this name. A Prussian politician with this first name kept power by making melodramatic offers to resign, which persuaded Wilhelm I to retain him.
swap.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

question.text: This Hapsburg convened the Diet of Worms (VURMS) and Council of Trent as emperor from 1519 to 1558.
question.clue: He signed the Peace of Augsburg with the Schmalkaldic League and during the Italian Wars captured Francis I at the Battle of Pavia.

swap.text: Tilly's first defeat in the war was in this September 17, 1631 battle where Gustav Karlsson Horn executed one of the first troop shifts in modern warfare. Gustavus Adolphus's troops killed some 12,000 Imperial troops at this battle in Saxony.
swap.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.

question.text: After his excommunication during the investiture controversy, Emperor Henry IV made a pilgrimage to this castle to beg for readmission to the church. Henry allegedly waited at the gate of this castle for three days in the snow.
question.clue: The most famous visitor to this city fasted for three days outside its castle during a blizzard to beg for forgiveness from Pope Gregory VII.

swap.leadin: This dispute gets its name from the ceremony in which the symbolic ring and staff is presented to newly "elected" bishops and abbots.
swap.text: Name this 11th century controversy that arose between the Catholic Church and secular rulers over selections of high-ranking clergy member
swap.clue: This event was resolved with the Concordat of Worms, which stated that a man could grant power "by the lance" but not "by ring and staff."

question.text: This first king of the Ottonian dynasty gets his nickname from the legend that he was fixing birding nets when told that he had been elected King of Germany.
question.clue: His wife accompanied him on his campaigns building monasteries, one of which was their burial site of Quedlinburg.

swap.text: One of the Catholic leaders at White Mountain was the Count of Tilly, who, along with this man, was one of the key Hapsburg commanders during the Thirty Years War. This man lost the Battle of Lutzen to Gustavus Adolphus and was killed after contemplating defection to the Protestant side.
swap.answerHtml: Albrecht Wenzel Eusebius von Wallenstein [accept Albrecht von Waldstein]
swap.clue: At Lutzen, Swedish forces defeated this capable Bohemian general. Emperor Ferdinand II had this man killed when he seemed likely to defect to the Protestant side.

question.text: Earlier, in 1629, Ferdinand II had tried to enforce the "Ecclesiastical Reservation" of the Peace of Augsburg by issuing this edict.
question.clue: Maximilian von Trautmannsdorf's Points of Pirna attempted to reconcile one party who had been alienated by this declaration, which was defended vociferously in Paul Laymann's Pacis Composito.

swap.text: This league defeated at the Battle of Muhlberg was a militarized version of the earlier League of Torgau and was composed of Lutheran German princes who opposed Charles V.
swap.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

question.leadin: John of Bohemia, of Crecy fame, originally gave Charles IV this name, but Charles renamed himself in honor of Charles the Fair of France.
question.text: Give this name of several rulers of Prague, like Charles' Nepomuk-killing son. A beloved duke of this name was murdered by his not-so-good brother, Boleslaus the Cruel.
question.clue: This name was borne by the protege of Saint Ludmila who was killed after refusing to fight Henry the Fowler.

swap.leadin: The foremost early leader of this faction was Jacob of Mies, who preached at the University of Prague that the laity should receive the Eucharist in both bread and wine.
swap.text: Name this moderate faction that maintained amicable relations with the Roman Catholic Church, and emerged victorious over their rivals at the Battle of Lipany during the Hussite Wars.
swap.clue: The radical Taborites were opposed by this more moderate Hussite faction, who eventually broke with their brethren and fought on the side of the Catholics.

question.text: Frederick Barbarossa withdrew his support of Antipope Callixtus III after this 1176 battle, in which he was decisively defeated by Alberto da Guissano and the forces of the Lombard League.
question.clue: The carroccio, an oxen-drawn war wagon topped with a sacred altar, was used at this 1176 battle, which prompted its loser to sign the Treaty of Venice.

swap.leadin: Name some people and things with related -isms.
swap.text: This man discussed a Bethlehem Steel Company worker named Schmidt who was "like an ox" in his diatribe against rules of thumb in factories, The Principles of Scientific Management, a discipline that is sometimes called this man's -ism.
swap.clue: Another emperor with this name was defeated by the Lombard League at the Battle of Legnano.
